question: Which state government of India launched the 'Swanirbhar Nari' aimed at making the weavers of the state self-reliant?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Assam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Assam** state government launched the '**Swanirbhar Nari**' scheme.
 
• This initiative aims to make the **weavers** of the state **self-reliant**.
 
• The scheme focuses on promoting **handloom and weaving** activities in the state.
 
• Assam has a rich tradition of **weaving**, often referred to as the **‘Manchester of the East’** due to its vibrant handloom sector.
 
• The initiative is expected to boost the **economic status** of the weavers and ensure **sustainable livelihoods**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Bihar**__

 __
 
• **Bihar** is known for its historical sites and cultural heritage.
 
• The state has a significant role in the **Indian freedom struggle**.
 
• It is known for its production of **silk and handloom textiles**, especially from the Bhagalpur region.
 
 
 
• **Chhattisgarh**__
 __
 
• **Chhattisgarh** is known for its **mineral resources**.
 
• The state is rich in **tribal culture** and traditions.
 
• It is a major producer of **rice** and is often referred to as the **'Rice Bowl of India'**.
 
 
 
• **Jharkhand**__
 
 
• **Jharkhand** is known for its **mining industry**.
 
• The state is rich in **forests** and **tribal culture**.
 
• It has significant reserves of **coal, iron ore, copper ore, and bauxite**.
